newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses open mixed, dlr holds mark gains.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses open mixed, dlr holds mark gains.

text.p: European bourses were mixed after Wall Street's record-breaking run stuttered to a halt and despite the storming debut of Europe's biggest phone company Deutsche Telekom.
Germany's blue-chip DAX opened firm, then slipped as Germany's major telecommuncations operator joined the 30-share index the day after its debut with a weighting of 4.5 percent.
French shares hovered around their opening levels, looking for direction, while British shares weakened a few points after erasing initial gains.
On foreign exchange markets, the dollar slipped back from its overnight highs against the yen but held on to its gains on the mark.
Bond markets saw German government bonds, or bunds, retain a firm bias in early trade, helping British government gilts to open 1/32 higher.

Worries about how long Wall Street's blistering rally can last continued to nag at European bourses after the Dow Industrials Average brought its eight consecutive record closes to an end on Monday with a one point decline.
In Germany, at least, the early market was dominated by Telekom. The DAX was up nearly seven points at one point, but just slipped below its opening level by 1035 GMT.
Telekom was down 1.48 marks to 32.42 after opening trade on Monday at 32.20.
The shares set bells ringing on the Tokyo stock market on Tuesday as Japanese investors and dealers rushed to trade the newly listed share as they had on Monday in New York and Frankfurt.
In London, shares crept higher at the start of business but soon turned negative on concerns about Wall Street and caution ahead of next Tuesday's British budget.

"We're so close to the budget, I don't think we'll do much. There seems to be a firmer bias," said one dealer. "But without a lead from the U.S. this afternoon, we could end on either side of unchanged."

The utility sector was likely to remain in the forefront amid rising takeover speculation after the Wall Street Journal said London Electricity may be the target of a 1.2 billion pound ($2 billion) offer from Entergy Corp of the United States.
French shares opened slightly lower and moved both sides of Monday's close before settling a few points down.
Dealers said the market lacked direction and the blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 3.57 points at 2,225.24 by 1035 GMT.
Eurotunnel was off 1.92 percent but off its lows after an overnight fire in the rail tunnel between Britain and France injured 34 people and forced the tunnel to halt operations.
Eurodisney fell 2.6 percent to 11.15 francs despite the company reporting a 77 percent rise in 1995/96 profits. The Paris theme park operator said it was not yet out of the woods.
The dollar was steady against the mark after Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said the German central bank would welcome a more stable and stronger dollar.
Earlier reports quoting him as saying he saw no reason for the dollar to rise at the moment were a misunderstanding, he told reporters late on Monday.
"The last thing the Bundesbank officials want is a firmer deutschmark," said Nigel Richardson, senior international economist at Yamaichi International.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 111.49 yen and 1.5033 marks, compared with 111.29 yen and 1.4996 marks in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1100 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 5.4 points at 3,956.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 3.57 points at 2,225.24.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 0.82 points at 2,764.66.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed easier at $378.30 against $379.10 on Monday afternoon and $379.70 in the morning. Silver was down two cents at $4.88.
